justification: Inspected `src/main/java/org/apache/commons/io/input/ByteBufferCleaner.java` (116 lines). The class is package-private and narrowly focused on one concern: selecting a JVM-specific cleaner (`Java8Cleaner` or `Java9Cleaner`) and exposing only two static operations, `clean(ByteBuffer)` and `isSupported()`. Its two nested implementations support the same single responsibility rather than separate features. The tests in `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/io/input/ByteBufferCleanerTest.java` and the callers in `BufferedFileChannelInputStream.java` and `MemoryMappedFileInputStream.java` use it only as a shared byte-buffer cleanup utility, with no evidence of multiple independent responsibilities or excessive method count.
